fault_notes: The customer reports persistent crackling on the landline, affecting both incoming and outgoing calls. The agent leaves two separate unexplained silences: the first lasts 55 seconds, and the second begins after the line-fault update, with no hold announcement beforehand and no acknowledgement or thanks afterward. [noconfirm added on saving: the fault is booked for a technician and the agent never confirms it is fixed. This version replaces gpt_10_noconfirm, which had only one silence.] [noname added after grading: the agent never says "Ibrahim" or "Hassan"; missed when saving.]

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net. My name is Sophie. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi, I'm having trouble with my landline. There's a crackling noise whenever I try to make a call.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm sorry about that. I can check the line and help work out what's causing the noise. Could I have your full name, please?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's Ibrahim Hassan.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. For security, could you confirm the first line of your registered address and your postcode?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's 24 Willow Road, and the postcode is B12 8LP.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's matched, thank you. I'll open your account and check the landline service details.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's been doing it since yesterday evening. It was fine before that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks for explaining. I'll check whether there are any known faults affecting your telephone line.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've tried a few calls this morning, and the crackling is there every time.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does the noise happen as soon as you pick up the handset, or only after you dial a number?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's there as soon as I pick it up. I can hear it before I dial.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That helps. Are you using a corded telephone or a cordless handset?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's a corded phone. The handset connects directly to the wall socket.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Do you have broadband equipment or a microfilter connected to the same telephone socket?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've got broadband through a router, and there's a small filter plugged into the socket.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could you check whether the filter or the telephone cable looks loose or damaged?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've had a look. Nothing seems damaged, and both plugs feel secure.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: All right. I'll run a remote line check and see if it reports a fault.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, because I need the landline for calls to my family, so I'd like to get it sorted.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course. I'll check the line test results and the service history.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks. It makes conversations quite difficult when the noise gets loud.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can understand that. I'll see what the test can tell us before we decide on the next step.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All right. Let me know what it shows.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm checking that now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello? Are you still there? It's been quiet for a while.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I'm here. The check is taking a little longer than expected. I'll continue looking at the results.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right. I wasn't sure whether the call had dropped.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The call is still connected, and I'm reviewing the diagnostic information.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay. I just don't want to have to start all over again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You won't need to repeat the details. I've got the information you've given me, and I'll continue from here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks. The noise is still there now, if that helps.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is useful to know. Is it a steady hiss, a crackle, or more like a buzzing sound?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's a crackling sound, almost like paper being crumpled. Sometimes it gets louder and then settles down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does it happen on incoming calls as well, or have you only noticed it when making outgoing calls?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Both. My brother called earlier, and I could hear the same crackling while we were talking.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That suggests it's not limited to outgoing calls. Have you tried disconnecting the broadband filter and reconnecting it?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Not yet. I checked that it was secure, but I haven't unplugged it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's try that. Unplug the telephone and filter, then reconnect the filter first and the phone afterward.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All right, give me a moment. I've unplugged them.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Reconnect the filter first, make sure it's seated properly, and then plug the telephone back in.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Done. I've plugged everything back in. I'll pick up the handset now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Go ahead. Can you still hear the crackling on the line?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it's still there. I can hear it quite clearly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Since reconnecting the filter hasn't helped, I'll check the line test again and see what it reports.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Honestly, it's getting frustrating. I've spent most of the morning trying to get a clear call.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm sorry it's been so disruptive. I'll make sure we follow this through rather than leave you with the same problem.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I appreciate that. I just need to know what happens next.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The remote check indicates a possible line fault. I'll review the available options for getting the physical line tested.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that mean someone needs to come out to the house?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A technician may need to inspect the line if the remote checks can't isolate the fault. I'll check whether we can arrange a visit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's fine. I'd rather have it checked properly than keep putting up with the noise.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is the telephone socket easy to access, or is it behind heavy furniture?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's easy to reach. The socket is on the wall beside the living room table.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's helpful. I'll check the diary and see what appointment windows are available.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Could it be sometime this week? I use the phone quite often.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'll look for the earliest available option. I can see a Thursday morning appointment window at the moment.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thursday morning should be fine. What time would they arrive?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The available window is between eight in the morning and midday. The technician will attend within that window.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All right, please book that. I can make sure someone is home.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'll arrange the Thursday visit and add the details about the persistent crackling noise and the unsuccessful filter check.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you. Please make sure they know it's affecting incoming calls too.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I've included that both incoming and outgoing calls are affected, and that the noise is present as soon as you pick up the handset.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good. That should give them a better idea of what to look for.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The appointment is booked for Thursday between eight and twelve. Please keep the telephone socket accessible for the technician.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No problem. Will I receive a confirmation message?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, a confirmation should arrive by text shortly. If anything changes, we'll use the contact details on your account to notify you.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All right. I hope the technician can get it fixed because the crackling is really annoying.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand. We've completed the initial checks and arranged the next step, so the technician can investigate the line fault in person.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks for arranging it. Is there anything else I should do before Thursday?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: There's nothing else you need to change. Keep the phone and filter connected as normal, and let the technician know if the noise changes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'll leave everything as it is and explain what I've noticed when they arrive.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we finish, is there anything else I can help you with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that's everything. Hopefully the line will be clear again after the visit.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net. We've booked the technician for Thursday morning, and I hope we can get the line working clearly again soon. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks for your help. Goodbye.
